questions.prompt: Two agonists produce the same maximum response in the same assay. Drug A has an EC50 of 2 nM and drug B an EC50 of 20 nM. Which comparison is supported?

choices.a: A is more potent; their measured maximal efficacy is equal.
choices.b: B is more potent because its EC50 is larger.
choices.c: A necessarily has a higher maximum response.

questions.explanation: A reaches half of its maximal response at a lower concentration. Equal measured maximum responses indicate equal maximal efficacy in this assay.
questions.learning_objective: Distinguish EC50-based potency from maximal efficacy.

questions.prompt: In a graded concentration-response experiment, which measurement describes the greatest response a drug can produce in that preparation?
questions.explanation: Emax is the maximal observed response. EC50 describes the concentration associated with half-maximal response; elimination half-life is a pharmacokinetic measure.
questions.learning_objective: Identify Emax as the maximal effect in a specified system.

questions.prompt: In a simple equilibrium assay, a reversible antagonist competes with an agonist at the same receptor site. Enough agonist can be added to overcome the blockade. What change is expected in the agonist curve?

choices.a: A lower maximum that cannot be restored
choices.b: A leftward shift with unchanged maximum
choices.c: A rightward shift with unchanged maximum

questions.explanation: More agonist is needed for a given response, but sufficient agonist can restore the original maximum under these stated conditions.
questions.learning_objective: Predict surmountable competitive antagonism in a simplified equilibrium model.

questions.prompt: A reversible competitive antagonist is present at a fixed concentration. If you keep increasing the agonist concentration, what happens to the response?

choices.a: It stays capped below the original maximum.
choices.b: It climbs back to the original maximum, but only at higher agonist concentrations.
choices.c: It falls toward zero as the receptors saturate.
choices.d: It does not change, because the antagonist has already bound.

questions.explanation: Binding is reversible and both drugs compete for the same site, so enough agonist outcompetes the antagonist. The full response returns, but more agonist is needed: the curve shifts right and Emax is unchanged.
questions.learning_objective: Predict that reversible competitive antagonism is surmountable and shifts the agonist curve right without lowering Emax.
